clue.text: Military assistant's funny idea — leg it!

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters of idea are rearranged

parts.note: to leg it is to run away, which is to decamp

explanation.surface: Someone has a silly notion and the cry is to run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges IDEA into AIDE; then comes DECAMP. The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is an officer who acts as a personal assistant to a senior commander.

clue.text: Before noon, doctor's rounds

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the time before noon
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A GP does the ward visits in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' looks like a doctor's visits but is the definition: rounds of ammunition. The 's on doctor stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, and its individual cartridges are called rounds.

clue.text: Impassive cathedral bigwig pocketing 500 per year

indicators.note: pocketing means the senior cleric holds the other letters inside him

parts.note: the dean is the head of a cathedral chapter
D is the Roman numeral for 500
PA is short for per annum, per year

explanation.surface: A senior churchman, poker-faced, quietly takes a modest annual sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, just as an impassive one does.

clue.text: Drinking with cryptic setter in capital location

parts.note: downing a drink is drinking it

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters of setter are jumbled

explanation.surface: Having a drink with the puzzle setter somewhere in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street, home of the Prime Minister, is a famous address in London, the UK capital.

clue.text: Order round for military group

parts.note: to command is to order
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A command is issued to a unit of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a unit of elite assault troops, so a fighting body of soldiers.

clue.text: Satisfied concerning poet's rhythm

parts.note: to have met a need is to have satisfied it
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Someone is content about how a poem scans.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the regular pattern of stressed syllables in verse.

clue.text: Understood husband is a fan of dark clothing

parts.note: 'I got it' means I understood it

explanation.surface: Someone realises their husband likes wearing black.
explanation.definitionFit: A goth belongs to a subculture known for black clothes and dark makeup.

clue.text: Not at home, on job in remote settlement

parts.note: someone out is not at home
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Someone away from home working in a far-flung place.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small settlement far from main centres.

clue.text: Extremists run into bad luck

indicators.note: into means the run letter is put inside the phrase for bad luck

parts.note: 'hard lines' is a British expression for bad luck
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Radicals have a stroke of misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD LINES is British slang for bad luck, said in sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardliners hold uncompromising, extreme positions.

clue.text: Catty remark from Ms Farrow? It hurts!

parts.note: Mia Farrow is an American actress
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A spiteful jibe aimed at an actress, who cries out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaow is the sound a cat makes, so literally a feline utterance.

clue.text: Someone who gives you drive in car without current tax

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the car goes around the other letters

parts.note: motor is an informal word for a car
I is the symbol for electric current
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A driver whose car has no road tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A motivator inspires ambition and energy, the drive to achieve.

clue.text: Deputy leader pens directive with a new order

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order is rearranging them

explanation.surface: A second-in-command writes an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a new order' rearranges PENS DIRECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice president deputises for a president, standing second in command.

clue.text: Soldiers relaxed around hotel in Harrow, say

parts.note: privates are ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: around means the word for relaxed surrounds the hotel letter

parts.note: cool means relaxed
H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Troops lounging around a hotel in a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrow' looks like a place or a farm tool; it is the famous school.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is a well-known fee-paying boys' school in north-west London, an example of a private school.

clue.text: Attacks team in Norfolk region

indicators.note: in means the team word sits inside the Norfolk name

parts.note: the Broads is an area of waterways in Norfolk, England
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports team goes on the offensive in East Anglia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are lakes and rivers in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a volley from all of a ship's guns, and figuratively a fierce verbal assault.

clue.text: Turncoat in retreat defied a general? Not completely

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back, so the letters are read backwards
only part of the phrase defied a general is used, so the letters lie within it

explanation.surface: A deserter disobeyed his commander while falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' takes EDAGENER from 'defied a general'; 'in retreat' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or side, as a turncoat changes allegiance.

clue.text: Lad keeping grass exactly right

indicators.note: keeping means the boy holds the other word inside

parts.note: a son is a lad
pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass

explanation.surface: A boy hiding some cannabis is quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an idiom for perfectly accurate.

clue.text: Utterly determined, this man will gamble around noon

parts.note: he'll is short for he will, said of this man

indicators.note: around means the gamble word wraps the noon letter

parts.note: to bet is to gamble

explanation.surface: A man resolves to place a wager at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell-bent describes someone recklessly set on a course of action.

clue.text: Sharp suit ruined with tea I dropped

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and put back in a new arrangement
dropped means the I letter is left out of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone spills tea on a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from SUIT, leaving SUT; 'ruined' rearranges SUT and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An astute person is shrewd and quick-witted, sharp in mind.

clue.text: Metal cover for sewer?

parts.note: sewer means one who sews, not a drain; the metal cap protects the needle-pushing finger

explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain, inviting a manhole cover; it is a person who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble is a small metal cap worn on a fingertip while sewing.

clue.text: Recall e.g. Michael Stipe losing one million

indicators.note: losing means one letter is lost from the phrase

parts.note: Michael Stipe is the singer of the band R.E.M., so an REM member
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Remembering a rock singer down on his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops one of the two adjacent Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: I bag one wild flower

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone picks an untamed bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The begonia is a popular flowering plant.

clue.text: Bob penning long chapter that's terrifying

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the coin holds the other letters

parts.note: bob was British slang for a shilling, an old coin
to pine is to long

explanation.surface: Someone writes a lengthy chapter of a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the slang name for a shilling, a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spine-chilling makes your blood run cold with fear.

clue.text: Is this caught in North India?

definitions.text: Is this caught in North India?

indicators.note: caught in means the letters are trapped within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking whether a language is picked up in northern India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' finds the answer inside 'North India'; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the main language of northern India, so it is what you would hear there.

clue.text: Information from all directions

explanation.surface: Reports arriving from everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: News is fresh information; it also spells the initials of the four compass points.

clue.text: Miss going to social events?

parts.note: a Miss is a young unmarried woman, here one making her first entrance into high society

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' could be a failure to attend; it is a young lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her formal debut in fashionable society.

clue.text: Wise guy?

parts.note: not a smart alec but the man surnamed Wise in a famous comedy double act

explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight-man partner of Eric Morecambe.

clue.text: Rudimentary building in Slough

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off

explanation.surface: A basic hut in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also an English town, a tempting reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a plain outbuilding; to shed skin is to slough it off.

clue.text: Parliament organised a sit-in — these people may demand regime change

definitions.text: these people may demand regime change

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly in some countries, such as Japan

indicators.note: organised means put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: MPs stage a protest demanding a change of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges A SIT-IN into ITIANS. 'Regime' is a diet plan, not a government.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietitians are nutrition experts who prescribe eating plans, so change a regimen.
